zones.notes: Mandatory tread protection from Day 1 through cleanup. Ram Board Stair Armor or equivalent non-slip protection. Standard plastic sheeting on treads is EXTREME FALL HAZARD per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2. Low-tack Safe-Release tape for securing. Covers riser face bottom edge, tread surface, and bullnose in one piece.
Drop cloth runners at landing areas to protect finished floors from drips and spills.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to heavy_mask when walls are SS_PAINTED_*
zones.notes: Wall masking along stringer top edge when spraying. Not needed for brush method when walls are unfinished (typical NC).

protection_zones_analysis.conditional_protection_note: Tread protection is UNCONDITIONAL — always required regardless of method or any other condition. Floor protection is conditional on floor_type. Wall masking is conditional on application_method = spray. Tread protection is the single most critical safety requirement in stair painting — plastic sheeting on treads is an extreme fall hazard.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Treads are above and below each riser. Treads may be stain-grade or floor-rated coating — always different from trim enamel. Treads are NOT painted in this spec (future SF_STAIR_TREAD_NC). Riser-to-tread edge masking required when treads are already finished or stain-grade.

Stringer meets wall at continuous linear joint. In NC, walls typically at SS_PRIMED_FIELD during stair trim work — no wall protection needed for brush. Stringer-to-wall caulk is a mandatory prep task for closed stringers.
Stringer connects to baseboard at top/bottom of flight. Typically same color/sheen. Baseboard handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.

adjacency_analysis.surface_reference: Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md v1.0 — stair surfaces are NEW, not yet in vocabulary
adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Stair component painting has two primary surfaces (risers and stringers) with dual UOM (EA and LF). Key adjacency is tread protection — treads are always protected, never painted in this spec. Stringer-to-wall caulk is a mandatory prep task, not just a protection relationship.

affected_conditions.notes: Landing floor protection required only when finished floors present. Subfloor requires no protection.

affected_conditions.modifier_notes: occupied_sensitive triggers OCC_SENSITIVE modifier 1.30x on protection tasks per Modifier_Registry
affected_conditions.notes: Additional protection when occupied. Rare in NC context.
Lead-safe practices when applicable. Rare in NC (post-1978) but possible in gut renovation.
Temperature affects dry times and open time. Stairwells may lack HVAC in NC — temperature varies by floor level.

valid_input_states.rationale: Combined prime+paint spec. SS_BARE (uncoated riser/stringer) requires full primer coat — primer type driven by substrate. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY (standard NC — trim arrives pre-primed from mill) skips primer, lighter prep.

output_state.rationale: Output state varies by sheen configuration dimension. Semi-gloss is default for risers (toe-kick scuff resistance).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Typical NC: walls at SS_PRIMED_FIELD — no protection for brush. When walls SS_PAINTED_*: masking required for brush near wall edge and always for spray.

Treads ALWAYS protected regardless of state. May be stain-grade (never painted), may be subfloor (painted last), or may be finished. Protection is unconditional per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

required_paintscope_keys.catalog_status: PROPOSED — derivable from geometry system rake_length

Wall masking along stringer edge (spray only)

proposed_new_keys.justification: Component spec needs its own surface key. Value may equal PS_META.STAIRWELL.RISERS from geometry system.

proposed_new_keys.justification: No existing key for painted stringer measurement. PS_SURFACE_SF.STAIRWELL_WALL_STRINGER covers wall behind stringer, not the stringer board itself.
No existing key for this edge relationship. Closed stringers only.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Riser meets tread at top and bottom edges. Treads are NOT painted in this spec — they are either stain-grade, subfloor, or painted last by future SF_STAIR_TREAD_NC. Riser-to-tread edge masking required when treads are already finished.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: In NC, treads are typically subfloor during riser painting. Tread protection is for the tread surface itself, not for paint-to-paint edge.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Stringer meets wall at continuous linear junction. Stringer-to-wall caulk is mandatory for closed stringers — highly visible joint. Open stringers have no wall junction on exposed side.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Typical: walls at SS_PRIMED_FIELD. Caulk applied during prep phase.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Riser meets stringer at left and right edges (2 joints per riser). Riser-to-stringer caulk fills visible gaps at this junction. Both surfaces painted in this spec — typically same finish.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Caulk LF derived from riser_count × 2 × stairwell_width. No dedicated PaintScope key — derived quantity.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Stringer connects to baseboard at top/bottom of flight. Typically same finish group. Baseboard handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT. Stringer-to-baseboard caulk included in this spec per brief Q2 resolution.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Natural transition point. Painter doing stringer work is already on-site with caulk.

relevant_findings.topic: Dual UOM — EA for risers, LF for stringers
relevant_findings.finding: This spec uses two units of measure: risers are counted as EA (each), stringers are measured as LF (linear feet). Risers are flat vertical panels with uniform size within a flight — no size bucket variation needed. Riser surface area is derivable: riser_SF = stairwell_width × riser_height (typically 3.5 ft × 0.625 ft ≈ 2.2 SF). Stringers are linear trim comparable to baseboard, measured in LF.
relevant_findings.impact: Production rates must be expressed in two UOMs: hrs/EA for riser tasks, hrs/LF or LF/hr for stringer tasks.

relevant_findings.topic: Combined prime+paint spec — primer is conditional on substrate_state
relevant_findings.finding: This spec includes both primer and finish coats, but primer is conditional. SS_BARE requires full primer coat (substrate-driven selection). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer — factory primer is transit protection. This matches SF_WINDOW_INT_NC pattern. Rationale: stairway work is a self-contained zone with dedicated staging, shared tread protection, and same-session execution.
relevant_findings.impact: Module structure must support both workflows. Prime module is conditional. Two variant round configs: with/without primer.

relevant_findings.topic: Substrate drives primer chemistry — 5 distinct primer paths
relevant_findings.finding: MDF cut/routed edges: solvent-based sealer (Zinsser BIN Shellac, KILZ Original) — water-based causes irreversible fiber swelling. MDF factory faces: high-build latex (BM Enamel Underbody 217). Poplar: stain-blocking primer MANDATORY (BM Prime Lock Plus). Hardwood: tannin-blocking primer (BM Prime Lock Plus, SW Extreme Block). Paint-grade plywood: standard primer-sealer (Zinsser Bulls Eye 1-2-3). MDF requires TWO-STEP prime: edge seal (solvent) then face prime (latex).
relevant_findings.impact: Materials Manager must include 5 substrate-driven primer systems. SOP must have substrate-conditional primer tasks. MDF edge sealing is a separate mandatory task before latex primer.

relevant_findings.topic: Canonical painting sequence — stringers before risers
relevant_findings.finding: Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2: Stringers are position #4 in the 9-position canonical sequence, risers are position #8. Within every module phase (prep, prime, finish), stringer tasks MUST precede riser tasks. Rationale: painting stringers first avoids contact with wet riser surfaces when moving between treads.
relevant_findings.impact: SOP must enforce stringer-before-riser ordering in every module. Task sequencing is non-negotiable.

relevant_findings.topic: Tread protection is non-negotiable safety requirement
relevant_findings.finding: Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2: 'Tread protection must begin before any painting starts and remain in place until the very final phase.' Ram Board Stair Armor is industry standard — covers riser face bottom edge, tread surface, and bullnose in one piece with Spill Guard and Tread-Trac grip strips. Standard plastic sheeting on treads is an EXTREME FALL HAZARD. Tread protection is first task in setup, last task in cleanup (or deferred if railing/tread work follows).
relevant_findings.impact: Setup module starts with tread protection. Cleanup module ends with protection removal. Protection remains through ALL phases. Safety-critical — no exceptions.

relevant_findings.topic: Height/access modifiers — risers H1, stringers use stairwell access modifiers
relevant_findings.finding: Risers always use H1 (1.0x) — painter stands on adjacent treads, always accessible. Stringers use stairwell access modifiers from PaintScope_Stairwell_Geometry_System based on PS_STAIRWELL.MAX_WORKING_HEIGHT_FT: step_ladder (≤12 ft)=1.3x, extension_ladder (≤18 ft)=1.6x, scaffolding (≤24 ft)=2.0x, lift (≤28 ft)=2.5x, tall_lift (28+ ft)=2.8x. For stair component work (this spec), access modifier alone applies to stringers. For stairwell drywall/ceiling work (separate specs), access modifiers ADD TO standard height modifiers.
relevant_findings.impact: Estimation Engineer applies H1 to all riser tasks, stairwell access modifier to all stringer tasks. Access modifiers do NOT stack with height modifiers for stair component work.

relevant_findings.topic: Open vs closed stringers — production rate impact
relevant_findings.finding: Open stringers have notched profile visible from exposed side, following tread/riser pattern. They have significantly more surface area and complex geometry compared to closed (flat board against wall) stringers. Production rate for open stringers: 1.3-1.5x that of closed stringers. Open stringers have stringer-to-wall caulk only on wall side; exposed side has no wall junction.
relevant_findings.impact: stringer_type is a configuration dimension. Production rates must include open stringer multiplier. Caulk tasks are conditional on closed stringers.

relevant_findings.topic: QT2 prohibited — stairways are scrutinized surfaces
relevant_findings.finding: Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1: stairways are scrutinized, prominent surfaces. QT2 is not applicable. Minimum quality tier is QT3.
relevant_findings.impact: Spec configuration_dimensions must prohibit QT2. Only QT3, QT4, QT5 are valid.

relevant_findings.topic: Finish material systems — reuse from trim spec (QT-driven)
relevant_findings.finding: Same SYS_FF_ finish systems as SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT and SF_WINDOW_INT_NC. QT3: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (100% acrylic enamel). QT4: SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (waterborne alkyd). QT5: SYS_FF_PREMIUM (premium urethane enamel). Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005 from trim spec).
relevant_findings.impact: Reuse existing SYS_FF_ IDs. No new finish systems needed.

relevant_findings.topic: Interstage is universal at ALL quality tiers
relevant_findings.finding: Same as trim and window specs. Interstage runs after every coat except the final coat. Sanding discipline: QT3=spot sand only (nibs, rough spots), QT4=full 220 grit, QT5=thorough 220-320 grit. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD 15.4.1).
relevant_findings.impact: Interstage module present at all QTs. Sanding discipline varies by QT.

relevant_findings.topic: Riser surface area derivable from geometry system
relevant_findings.finding: Riser width = stairwell width (PS_META.STAIRWELL.WIDTH_FT). Riser height is standard ~7.5 inches (0.625 ft). Riser SF per unit = stairwell_width × riser_height. Typical: 3.5 ft × 0.625 ft ≈ 2.2 SF per riser. Risers are uniform within a flight — no size bucket variation.
relevant_findings.impact: Material coverage derived from riser count × SF per riser. Production rates in hrs/EA based on this typical SF.

relevant_findings.topic: Access staging overhead — 15-40% of project time
relevant_findings.finding: Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 5.6: stairway projects have 15-40% of total time consumed by access staging (moving ladders, platforms, tools up/down stairs). This is a project-level overhead, not a per-task modifier.
relevant_findings.impact: Estimation Engineer should note access staging overhead for project-level estimation. Not modeled as task-level modifier.

condition_drivers.notes: QT drives finish material system (recommendations), sheen restrictions, sanding between coats, inspection scrutiny. Does NOT drive primer selection (substrate-driven). Does NOT affect application quality baseline.
Brush is default for stair component detail work. Spray requires extensive tread/wall masking but faster application.
Substrate drives primer chemistry. MDF: two-step (edge seal + face prime). Poplar: stain-blocking MANDATORY. Hardwood: tannin-blocking. Plywood: standard sealer.
SS_BARE: full primer coat required, heavier prep. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: skip primer, scuff sand only.

Open stringers: 1.3-1.5x production rate multiplier, notched profile. Closed stringers: baseline rate, flat board. Stringer-to-wall caulk applies to closed stringers only (and wall side of open stringers if present).
Sheen/QT gate: satin at QT3+, semi-gloss at QT4+, gloss at QT5 only. Semi-gloss is default (toe-kick scuff resistance).

quality_differences.qt3: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC — 100% acrylic enamel (ProClassic WB, Regal Select)
quality_differences.qt4: SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE — waterborne alkyd (BM Advance, SW Pro Industrial WB Alkyd)
quality_differences.qt5: SYS_FF_PREMIUM — premium urethane enamel (Emerald Urethane, Scuff-X)

quality_differences.qt3: Spot sand only — visible nibs, rough spots
quality_differences.qt4: Light full sand — 220 grit, entire surface for adhesion
quality_differences.qt5: Thorough full sand — 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern

quality_differences.qt3: Quick glance at 6ft distance — obvious defects only
quality_differences.qt4: Systematic scan at 3ft — all visible defects marked
quality_differences.qt5: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance
2-3 finish coats (3+ typical for brush/roll per FFD 15.10.3)

quality_differences.qt3: Same baseline — no drips, sags, holidays, lap marks (NOT tiered)

failure_modes.cause: Using water-based primer without tannin-blocking properties on bare hardwood
failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS use tannin-blocking primer on bare hardwood. BM Prime Lock Plus, SW Extreme Block, or shellac-based primer. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult — tannin bleed re-emerges through multiple finish coats. Requires stripping to bare wood and using proper tannin-blocking primer.

failure_modes.failure: MDF fiber swelling on cut edges
failure_modes.cause: Applying water-based primer to raw MDF cut/routed edges before solvent-based sealer
failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS seal MDF edges with shellac-based (Zinsser BIN) or oil-based (KILZ Original) sealer FIRST. Two-step prime process for bare MDF. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 2 and Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.3.
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult — requires sanding back to substrate, fiber swelling is irreversible without aggressive sanding

failure_modes.cause: Using non-stain-blocking primer on bare poplar
failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS use stain-blocking primer on bare poplar. BM Prime Lock Plus, BM Fresh Start oil-based, or Zinsser BIN Shellac. MANDATORY, not optional. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1.
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult — bleed may re-emerge through multiple finish coats. Requires shellac-based primer to permanently block.

failure_modes.failure: Tread finish damage from inadequate protection
failure_modes.cause: Painting risers/stringers without proper tread protection, or using slippery plastic sheeting on treads
failure_modes.prevention: Mandatory tread protection from Day 1. Ram Board Stair Armor or equivalent non-slip protection. NEVER use plastic sheeting on treads — extreme fall hazard. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.
failure_modes.reversibility: Moderate to difficult — depends on damage extent. Damaged treads may require re-sanding and re-finishing.

failure_modes.cause: Over-application on vertical surfaces, material too thick, cold temperature slowing flow-out
failure_modes.prevention: Thin coats per waterborne philosophy. Proper brush loading. Risers are vertical surfaces — gravity pulls runs. Check for sags after moving to next riser. Application failure — NOT acceptable at ANY tier.
failure_modes.reversibility: Sand out when fully cured with rigid block. May require additional coat.

failure_modes.cause: Overworking waterborne product, wrong brush technique, material too thick or cold
failure_modes.prevention: Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD Section 15.3.1). Use quality brush with proper loading. Sand out marks between coats with rigid block.
failure_modes.reversibility: Addressable — sand between coats with rigid block and recoat

failure_modes.cause: Structural movement, seasonal expansion/contraction, poor caulk adhesion
failure_modes.prevention: Use quality paintable acrylic latex caulk. Apply after primer cure. Proper joint width (1/8 to 1/4 inch).
failure_modes.reversibility: Easy — re-caulk and touch-up. Part of interstage inspection.

failure_modes.cause: Oil-modified/alkyd products yellowing in UV-deprived environments
failure_modes.prevention: Use non-yellowing waterborne products for enclosed stairwells. SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (100% acrylic) does not yellow. Verify product PDS for yellowing resistance.
failure_modes.reversibility: Moderate — requires full recoat with non-yellowing product.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Dual material system — substrate-driven primer, QT-driven finish
notes_for_materials_manager.content: This spec has TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven (MDF edge seal + face prime, poplar stain-blocking, hardwood tannin-blocking, plywood standard). (2) Finish systems are QT-driven (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, SYS_FF_PREMIUM). Same pattern as SF_WINDOW_INT_NC.

MDF cut/routed edges: Solvent-based sealer (Zinsser BIN Shellac, KILZ Original). MDF factory faces: High-build latex (BM Enamel Underbody 217, ProClassic Undercoater). Poplar: Stain-blocking primer MANDATORY (BM Prime Lock Plus, BM Fresh Start oil-based). Hardwood: Tannin-blocking primer (BM Prime Lock Plus, SW Extreme Block). Plywood: Standard primer-sealer (Zinsser Bulls Eye 1-2-3, KILZ 2). Factory-primed: No primer needed.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Finish material systems — reuse from trim spec
notes_for_materials_manager.content: Same SYS_FF_ finish systems as SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT and SF_WINDOW_INT_NC. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

Ram Board Stair Armor is industry standard. Alternatives: rosin paper + masonite (premium), Trimaco Stay Put Canvas Plus. Standard plastic sheeting PROHIBITED on treads (extreme fall hazard). Low-tack Safe-Release tape for securing all tread protection.

Paintable acrylic latex caulk for: (1) Stringer-to-wall junction (closed stringers — continuous linear joint), (2) Riser-to-stringer junction (2 joints per riser). Caulk quantity: stringer-to-wall LF + (riser_count × 2 × riser_width) for riser-to-stringer joints.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Coverage rates for risers and stringers
notes_for_materials_manager.content: Risers: coverage from EA count × riser SF each (typically 2.2 SF per riser). Stringers: 1 LF ≈ 1 SF per PDCA standard for linear trim. Typical coverage: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface.
QT3: 220 grit for spot sanding only. QT4: 220 grit for full surface. QT5: 220-320 grit for full surface. Rigid sanding blocks mandatory for defect removal (FFD 15.4.1).

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Module structure is combined prime+paint with dual UOM
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: SETUP → INITIAL_PREP → [PRIME (conditional)] → [INTERSTAGE] → FINISH_COAT_1 → INTERSTAGE → FINISH_COAT_2 → FINAL_INSPECT → CLEANUP. Prime module runs only when substrate_state = SS_BARE. Tasks within each module split by component: stringer tasks first, then riser tasks (canonical sequence).

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Canonical sequence — stringers before risers in every phase
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: Within each module (prep, prime, finish), stringer tasks MUST precede riser tasks. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2: stringers at position #4, risers at position #8.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Tread protection is the FIRST and LAST task
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: First task in SETUP: install tread protection. Last task in CLEANUP: remove tread protection (or defer if railing/tread work follows). Protection remains through ALL phases.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Prep tasks vary by substrate type
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: Bare MDF: sand faces 220, sand edges 120, clean dust, fill holes, caulk joints, MDF edge seal. Bare poplar: light sand 150-180, clean, fill, caulk. Bare hardwood: sand 150-220, clean, fill, caulk. Bare plywood: sand 150-180, clean, fill, caulk. Factory-primed: scuff sand 150-180, clean, fill, caulk.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Two caulk joint types in initial prep
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: (1) Stringer-to-wall caulk — continuous joint for closed stringers, mandatory. (2) Riser-to-stringer caulk — 2 joints per riser. Both use paintable acrylic latex caulk. Caulk after fill and sand, before primer.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: MDF edge sealing is a separate mandatory task
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: For bare MDF: edge seal (solvent-based) MUST run BEFORE latex primer. Two-step prime: (1) TSK_STRS_SEAL_MDF_EDGES, (2) TSK_STRS_PRIME_FACES. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges.

Examples: TSK_STRS_TREAD_PROTECT, TSK_STRS_FLOOR_PROTECT, TSK_STRS_FILL_FASTENERS, TSK_STRS_CAULK_STRINGER_WALL, TSK_STRS_CAULK_RISER_STRINGER, TSK_STRS_SAND_PREP, TSK_STRS_SEAL_MDF_EDGES, TSK_STRS_PRIME_STRINGER, TSK_STRS_PRIME_RISER, TSK_STRS_BRUSH_FINISH_STRINGER_1, TSK_STRS_BRUSH_FINISH_RISER_1.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Interstage is universal at ALL quality tiers
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: Interstage runs after every coat except the final coat. Tasks: clean area, inspect coat, sand (spot or full per QT), patch/repair defects, sand patches, spot coat. Scrutiny level is qt_scaled.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Application philosophy for vertical riser surfaces
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: Waterborne philosophy (FFD 15.3.1): Apply, tip once, walk away. Risers are vertical — gravity pulls runs. Thin coats essential. Proper brush loading critical.
At QT5 with brush/roll (especially gloss), 3+ coats may be needed per FFD 15.10.3. Add additional FINISH_COAT + INTERSTAGE cycle as variant.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Dual UOM production rates — hrs/EA for risers, LF/hr for stringers
notes_for_estimation_engineer.content: Risers use EA-based rates (flat vertical panel, ~2.2 SF each). Stringers use LF-based rates (linear trim, similar to baseboard). Rates comparable to trim rates from Production Rate Reference System 3.

Risers are flat vertical panels ~2.2 SF each. Brush finish estimate: ~0.05-0.08 hrs/EA per coat. Prep rate: ~0.03-0.05 hrs/EA. Doctrine Section 9.2 confirms 'production rates similar to trim' but provides no per-EA rates.
Closed stringers: use baseboard trim rates as baseline (80-90 LF/hr brush finish). Open stringers: apply 1.3-1.5x multiplier for notched profile complexity.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Height/access modifiers — different for risers vs stringers
notes_for_estimation_engineer.content: Risers: H1 (1.0x) always. Stringers: stairwell access modifiers from geometry system based on max_working_height. Access modifiers do NOT stack with height modifiers for stair component work.
Closed stringer: 1.0x baseline. Open stringer: 1.3-1.5x multiplier. Open stringers have notched profile with more surface area.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Access staging overhead — 15-40% of project time
notes_for_estimation_engineer.content: Per doctrine Section 5.6: 15-40% of total time consumed by access staging. Project-level overhead, not per-task modifier.
QT3=1.00, QT4=1.30, QT5=1.50. Apply to inspection, repair, and sanding tasks. Do NOT apply to application rate.
Ram Board Stair Armor install: ~2-3 min per tread (14 treads = ~30-45 min). Removal: ~1-2 min per tread. Binary task (same at all QTs).

inherited_research_corrections.impact: No dry time references in materials or sop_modules — refer to PDS

uncertainties.topic: QT3 default with semi-gloss default tension
uncertainties.description: Brief sets QT3 default and semi-gloss default. But sheen/QT gate says semi-gloss requires QT4+. Two defaults are incompatible.
uncertainties.current_approach: Proceeding with both defaults as stated. Spec enforces sheen/QT gate at runtime — QT3 with semi-gloss rejected, satin offered.

uncertainties.description: Brief specifies 1.3-1.5x range. No canonical doctrine value. Exact multiplier depends on notch depth and profile.
